steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C). Spray a 9x13-inch casserole dish with cooking spray.
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook elbow macaroni in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Drain.
While the macaroni is cooking, slowly melt butter in a large pot over low heat. Stir in evaporated milk and pepper; cook until heated through.

Whisk eggs in a bowl until smooth. Whisk in about 1/2 cup of the hot evaporated milk mixture, 1 tablespoon at a time, until thoroughly incorporated. Whisk egg mixture back into the saucepan and continue to heat gently, whisking constantly, until milk mixture almost comes to a simmer and the sauce thickens.

Gently mix in cooked macaroni and salt until combined. Spoon 1/4 of the macaroni mixture in a layer into the bottom of the prepared casserole dish and top with 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese. Repeat layers three more times, then sprinkle paprika over the casserole.
Bake in the preheated oven until bubbling, about 20 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Southern Macaroni and Cheese Pie
raw_recipe.description: Southern mac and cheese pie is a creamy comfort food made with macaroni, evaporated milk, and lots of Cheddar. You’ll find it at church dinners and socials.

review.reviewBody: Two things that are important to the end result: use canned milk; and follow the directions for the milk/egg mixture: For some who may not know, it is mandatory to add a little of the heated milk to the beaten eggs as described to 'condition' the eggs to the hotter temperature. If you just 'dump' the cold eggs into the hot mixture, the yolks will cook, and you will have a mess. Stir constantly as milk has a tendency to scald if the temperature is too hot. Once the mixture begins to form tiny bubbles around the edges in the pot, it is simmering. Do not boil. continue to stir constantly and, if necessary, remove from heat and lower temperature. When the milk/egg mixture coats the spoon, you are ready to proceed to the next step, in my opinion. And, if you don't understand the term 'coating the spoon' it means that when you take the spoon from the pot, a coating of the mixture should remain on the spoon. You don't want the sauce to be thick - it will reduce/thicken as it bakes in the oven. This is my go-to mac n cheese recipe henceforth. I had been looking for a recipe that incorporated eggs, and I found perfection in this recipe--at least for my taste. Absolutely the best mac n cheese I have ever made. Thanks to dameionec for shartin!

It was delicious. I made a couple of changes. 1. I doubled the recipe and cooked it in an aluminum foil pan, and cooked it on a large cookie sheet. 2. I added Mozzarella, Romano, Provolone, Parmesan, and one extra cup of Sharp Cheddar cheese, or Italian cheese combination. After combining the eggs into the milk, when the milk and eggs began to thicken is when I added Italian bread crumbs, and Italian cheese combination, removed it from the heat stirring until perfectly creamy Than add the macaroni to the cheese sauce and layered it, andsprinkled Paprika on top. 3. I also lowered the oven temperature to 400 Degree Fahrenheit and cooked it for an additional 20 to 45 minutes, keeping an eye on it, until it browned just right.

I made it the first time as described, but I had the weird egg mixture texture that some others referred to, even after tempering the eggs. Also, I thought that there wasn't enough macaroni. When I remade it, I increased the amount of macaroni to three and a half cups. I mixed the butter (not melted) in with the strained hot macaroni. While alternating the layers of the buttered macaroni and the cheese (ending with the cheese), I sprinkled the salt and pepper between each layer. Then, I just mixed the egg and milk at room temperature and poured them together into the pan with the macaroni and cheese. This turned out much better.

I have made this based on a South Carolina Maw Maw's recipe, and it is always delicious! You don't need to heat the milk at all for it to work. It's so easy! Cook the macaroni al dente, add in layers to a buttered dish mac, cheese, eg/milk mixture till you've used all ingredients. You can add anything you want: seasoning, mustard, even meat. I like to add a little dry mustard to the milk and or ham. You can even cook this in the crock pot Yuuuuummmmmm! Enjoy

I make this for every family gathering and for Sunday dinners occasionally. I add a pinch(1/2 teaspoon)of ground mustard and about a teaspoon of cayene pepper to brighten it up a tad. It's never too spicy for the kids and the seasoning is always perfect. I also cook my macaroni before baking and I boil them the night before and let them sit(undrained) overnight.

I used 2 eggs instead of 3 and I mixed-up cheese, sauce and noodles in a bowl before putting it in baking pan, than topped with more cheese. 
Turned out wonderful and so tastey. Thanks for yummy recipe.

I used 2 eggs, buttered bread crumbs on top and another cup of pasta. Baked in a casserole dish the way my Mother used to...delicious! I added a few more spices; onion and garlic powders. This will probably be my go-to recipe from now on.

A perfectly good Mac & cheese to fall back on or use as a base to get creative with. Not AMAZING on its own, but the kids will love it and the adults will eat it. Simple on-hand ingredients. I used 1 teaspoon of pepper because I figured I could always add more after if necessary (though I didn’t) and doubled the pasta because after using the 2 cups called for, they were absolutely swimming. I skipped the layering and just put all the cheese into the sauce, then added the pasta and once mixed, poured it all into the casserole dish. I added toasted breadcrumb topping. I am familiar with the concept of tempering eggs, so didn’t have any issues with scrambled bits or lumps. Easy, simple recipe.

I added seasoning to my milk mixture and also melted my cheese INTO the milk mixture. I assume everyone else is layering like it said but my brain cant get behind that. Its a great base mac chrese pie recipe. Add stewed tomatoes and breadcrumbs ontop for a little flare

Love this recipe but I add some things… I add some garlic powder to the milk mixture and I add 3/4 of a block of 8oz Velveeta cheese to the milk and create a cheese sauce. Also put some of the shredded cheese to the cheese sauce
I cut the black pepper to 1 teaspoon. The top was dried out. So, next time I'll cover the dish with foil. Will make again with tweaks.

Way too much pepper. I used half tablespoon and is still heavy. Of course depends on fresh ground or not and how fine. I will probably use 1 teaspoon next. I split into square pans. Very good simple flavor!
This is really good winter food! I may make it for cookouts, too. It’s fairly simple to make! Mmmmmm

Made this for dinner tonight, but mixed in some cooked bacon, mushroom and spinach. This looked absolutely delicious going into the oven, and while it still tasted nice I was disappointed with the sauce as it came out. It lost its velvety texture. Maybe I cooked it too long? Or the temp was too high? Will try again to see if I can get it to come out better.

I was afraid of the 1 tablespoon of pepper called for in this recipe and made myself double check the list of ingredients. I always read recipes where the pepper measurement was half that of the salt. I did taste the pepper in the finished dish, but my family members said it was fine, no need to change anything.
I have made this so many times that my son will no longer eat it. That’s ok, more for me! 😆

I followed the ingredients exactly, and all who ate it thought it was great! I baked it at 350 for 1/2 hr. (because I was baking a chicken as well) and then baked for 15 min. at 375 until it bubbled in the middle. Next time I will use a smaller dish though, as I would have liked the "pie" to be thicker... mine was only a little over an inch tall in the 9x13. This was exactly what I was looking for to have the texture and flavor that I was used to, thank you dameionec for this recipe!
